extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and patent practitioners admitted before the USPTO, Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and parties to USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 implementing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) based on a state-bar disbarment, describing procedural response requirements, punitive and interim measures (limited recognition/wind-up), publication/notification obligations, and reinstatement/cost rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 (reciprocal discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO is ordered for violation of the ethical standards set out in 37 C.F.R. §§10.23(a) and 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(5), based upon a disbarment by a duly constituted authority of a State (here, the State Bar of Texas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may exclude a practitioner when the Office of Enrollment and Discipline files a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 based on a state disciplinary order (example: February 18, 2009 order of the State Bar of Texas disbarring the respondent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file a timely response to the Notice and Order (40 days) under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner seeks to contest exclusion under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d), the practitioner must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information the practitioner believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the state would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informed the respondent of this deadline and the content required; failure to file such a response allows the Director to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and that exclusion is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to respond to the Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file the required response within the prescribed time (40 days), the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and that exclusion from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order finds respondent did not file a response and accordingly determined exclusion was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific misconduct examples supporting state-bar disbarment (grounds for discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar disbarred the practitioner for neglecting to file provisional, utility, and Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) applications on behalf of a client; not complying with reasonable requests for information from the client about the status of those applications; not refunding an unearned, advance payment of a $10,700 fee upon termination of representation; and not timely furnishing to that state's Chief Disciplinary Counsel's Office a response or other information as required by the Texas Rules of Disciplinary Procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual findings illustrate ethical violations (client neglect, failure to communicate, failure to refund unearned fees, failure to respond to disciplinary inquiries) that can be the basis for reciprocal discipline by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for wind-up period (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date of the Final Order to wind up client business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is an interim, time-limited permission to the excluded practitioner solely to enable orderly wind-up of client matters and compliance with withdrawal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to wind up client business and withdraw from employment per 37 C.F.R. §10.40
rubrics_metrics.description: During the limited recognition period the respondent is directed to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal and wind-up must comply with the ethical/procedural requirements of §10.40 (e.g., notice to clients, return of papers/unearned fees as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limited recognition is solely for winding up existing matters; accepting new matters during this period is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) Director shall publish the Final Order and shall publish the specified notice of exclusion in the Official Gazette, including practitioner's name, registration number, grounds for the exclusion, statutory/regulatory citations, and where disciplinary decisions are posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice text is given in the Order; disciplinary decisions are posted at the OED Reading Room URL provided. Publication is part of the public record and notice function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public under 37 C.F.R. §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision ensures interjurisdictional communication of disciplinary actions and furthers reciprocal enforcement and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement obligations — compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for reinstatement must meet the regulatory requirements in §11.60 (procedural and substantive standards for seeking restoration of practice privileges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs (each party bears own costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No costs are assessed against either party by this Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/Certificate of Service requirements under 37 C.F.R. §11.11
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.11, and by regular first class mail to an alternate address where the OED Director believes respondent receives mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service of disciplinary notices and orders follows the procedures in §11.11 (addresses on file, certified mail, alternate service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: This disciplinary action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations identify the statutory/regulatory basis empowering the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline, publish notices, and notify other authorities.
